title: EditorImportPlugin provides weird errors when the generated file does not use save_path
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.4.1, 4.6.1. Tested on Windows.

### System information

Win11 - Godot 4.4.1.stable.mono

### Issue description

EditorImportPlugins whose `_import` methods do not create the expected resource file at `save_path` error, well, weirdly.

That is, it does not produce an immediate error that no file was populated at `save_path`, and instead causes an unusual re-import on focus loop that emits
```
  ERROR: core/io/file_access.cpp:1002 - Condition "f.is_null()" is true. Continuing.
```

For a while I didn't even know what was going on here. For some reason I didn't hit it and another team member of mine did (I had a cached file at the expected `save_path` which prevented re-import from happening).

However, updating to 4.6 gave me a better clue:
```
  ERROR: core/io/file_access.cpp:1002 - Condition "f.is_null()" is true. Continuing.
  ERROR: Cannot open file 'res://.godot/imported/en_us.json-f6ab5d7b2a19de1aeb109695bedf11f9.translation'.
  ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://.godot/imported/en_us.json-f6ab5d7b2a19de1aeb109695bedf11f9.translation.
```

Ultimately what appears to be going on is that when an editor plugin fails to create a resource at `save_path`, then the editor _does not_ emit a warning or error, and then tries to re-import the file whenever the editor window is focused (including when the editor is re-opened).

While this is ultimately user error (i.e. an issue with the custom `EditorImportPlugin`), the importer should perform a sanity check that a file was in fact created at `save_path` and issue an informative warning if not.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make a slightly broken importer plugin that saves to somewhere other than `save_path`.
2. Create a file it can import
3. Restart the editor

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

This is a very trivial project with just a label that translates a string. The plugin saves to `<original file without ext>.translation` instead of `save_path`, triggering the issue.

[editor_import.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26163999/editor_import.zip)
